name: Raga
description: District headquarters and main town of Kamle district, serving as the primary gateway and administrative hub for exploring the surrounding hills, forests, and river valleys of central Arunachal Pradesh.
facts: Headquarters of Kamle district, created in 2017 from parts of Lower and Upper Subansiri
Located approximately 44 km north of Ziro and about 100 km from Itanagar
Main population center and starting point for local tourism and cultural experiences among Nyishi communities
Coordinates from Wikipedia and geographic records

name: Kamle River
description: Major river after which the district is named, a tributary of the Subansiri, offering opportunities for rafting, angling, and scenic river journeys through forested hills.
facts: Namesake of Kamle district; joins the Subansiri River before reaching the Brahmaputra
District administration has organized angling and rafting expeditions to promote tourism
Scenic stretches suitable for eco-tourism and adventure activities
Flows through multiple circles including areas near Raga and Dollungmukh

name: Rach-Ratch Confluence
description: Confluence of the Kamle and Subansiri rivers near Dollungmukh, identified for potential river tourism development including boating and eco-tourism.
facts: Visited by Chief Minister Pema Khandu and officials in 2026 to assess river tourism potential
Part of a navigable stretch from the Subansiri Lower Hydroelectric Project site
Plans announced for master plan, yacht procurement, and sustainable marine/river tourism
Located in the Dollungmukh area of Kamle district

name: Godak Village
description: Village in Kamle district featuring lesser-known historic sites Tulum Sibla and Kuru Luktu, highlighted for cultural and heritage tourism potential.
facts: District Commissioner visited Tulum Sibla and Kuru Luktu sites to promote them as heritage destinations
Reflects deep-rooted local history and is promoted as a hidden gem for visitors
Suitable for cultural immersion and camping in surrounding areas
Part of the Nyishi cultural landscape of Kamle

name: Megdong Village
description: Rural village in Kamle district known for Nyishi tribal culture, traditional lifestyle, and community experiences under the Vibrant Village Programme.
facts: Hosted NCC cadets under Vibrant Village Programme for cultural exchange with Nyishi community
Residents primarily of the Dong title within the Nyishi tribe
Offers insights into traditional attire, customs, agriculture, and rural life amid hills
Promoted for rural tourism and homestay initiatives in the Kamle basin

name: Dollungmukh
description: Administrative circle and settlement near the Kamle-Subansiri confluence, serving as a base for river-related tourism and local community access.
facts: One of the five primary administrative circles of Kamle district
Proximity to Rach-Ratch confluence makes it relevant for emerging river tourism
Local residents involved in supporting hydroelectric and potential tourism projects
Part of the district's hilly and forested terrain

name: Kamporijo
description: Administrative circle in Kamle district with villages and river valleys, offering offbeat exploration of Nyishi landscapes and potential trekking or nature walks.
facts: One of the main administrative circles with a significant number of villages
Located in the central part of the district with forested hills
Suitable for cultural and nature-based visits away from major tourist circuits
Part of the areas from which Kamle district was formed

name: Gepen
description: Administrative circle and surrounding villages in Kamle, representing typical rural Nyishi settlements with scenic hill and forest surroundings for offbeat tourism.
facts: One of the five primary circles of Kamle district
Consists of multiple villages in hilly terrain
Offers potential for community-based tourism and nature experiences
Inhabited primarily by Nyishi communities

name: Palin
description: District headquarters and small hill station town of Kra Daadi, inhabited by the Nyishi tribe, with subtropical highland climate, scenic views, and access to surrounding forests and rivers.
facts: Headquarters of Kra Daadi district, carved from Kurung Kumey in 2015
Average elevation about 1080 metres; subtropical highland climate
Coordinates from official district website
Primary administrative and commercial hub; connected by road from Ziro, Koloriang and Itanagar

name: Yangte
description: Picturesque village and circle headquarters known for serene landscapes, lush hills, forests, and the nearby Living Stone (Palang Sangri) natural geological formation.
facts: Official tourist place listed by Kra Daadi district administration
Home to the 'Living Stone' or Palang Sangri natural sculpture site nearby
Coordinates from official district tourist page
Offers cultural immersion among Nyishi communities and nature walks

name: Tali
description: Charming remote village and ADC headquarters nestled in hills, known for tranquil ambiance, natural beauty, and proximity to Yangmi Waterfall.
facts: Official tourist place; remote circle headquarters about 90 km from Palin
Nearby Yangmi (or Yangmi Sedang) Waterfall is a highlighted natural attraction
Coordinates from official district tourist page
Ideal for nature lovers seeking isolation in the Eastern Himalayas

name: Gyapin
description: Tranquil village surrounded by mountains and greenery, featuring a hot spring and the scenic Pai Waterfall.
facts: Official tourist place listed by district administration
Known for a warm hot spring and Pai Waterfall cascading from rocky cliffs
Coordinates from official district tourist page
Offers relaxation and nature immersion in rural Nyishi landscape

name: Ha Village
description: Peaceful village surrounded by green hills, serving as a living cultural museum of Nyishi traditions, colorful attire, and customs blended with modern life.
facts: Official tourist place highlighting cultural heritage and scenic surroundings
Described as a living museum of Eastern Himalayan traditions
Coordinates from official district tourist page
Suitable for cultural experiences and peaceful rural stays

name: Yangmi Waterfall
description: Mesmerizing multi-step waterfall (also known as Yangmi Sedang or Seven Sisters) near Tali/Yarda area, cascading down rocky cliffs amid lush forests.
facts: Highlighted on official Tali tourist page as a natural wonder
Also referred to as Yangmi Sedang or Seven Sister Waterfall near Yarda/Serdang village
Popular among locals and emerging eco-tourism site on the way to Tali
Scenic five-step or multi-cascade falls suitable for nature photography and visits

name: Palang Sangri (Living Stone)
description: Unique natural geological formation and living stone near Yangte, with mythological significance among Nyishi people, featuring natural sculptures and caves.
facts: Also called Living Stone or Pelang Sangri; discovered/highlighted by local groups near Yangte
Natural meta-sedimentary rock formations with dolomite; local folklore of blessings
Located in Langa Tata / Rayung Domchuk area about 10 km from Yangte HQ
Promoted as a natural heritage and potential tourist spot

name: Pai Waterfall
description: Breathtaking waterfall in Gyapin village cascading from rocky cliffs into a pool, especially impressive in the rainy season.
facts: Featured on official Gyapin tourist page
Forms a curtain of water; visitors can enjoy the pool at the base
Part of the natural attractions of Gyapin along with its hot spring
Accessible within the village surroundings

name: Palin River
description: Scenic river flowing through Palin area with pebble beaches, views of pine-covered hills, and potential for rafting, fishing, and picnics.
facts: Tributary of the Subansiri; flows through the Palin town area
Offers scenic views and is noted for rafting, fishing, and picnic spots
Hanging bridges mentioned in tourism descriptions of the area
Central to the district's riverine landscape

name: Chambang
description: Administrative circle known for rural beauty, forest trails, Nyishi villages, and traditional bamboo architecture in the hilly terrain.
facts: One of the seven circles of Kra Daadi with multiple villages
Noted in tourism guides for rural beauty and forest trails
Part of the Nyishi cultural landscape with traditional settlements
Accessible from Palin area for offbeat exploration

name: Tarak Lengdi
description: Area with viewpoint belt offering panoramic views of valleys, forests, and hills, suitable for birdwatching and gentle hikes.
facts: Mentioned in tourism sources as a viewpoint belt with valley panoramas
Administrative circle in the district
Offers opportunities for nature walks and photography amid green forests
Part of the lesser-visited landscapes of Kra Daadi

name: Pipsorang
description: Remote administrative circle near the border, representing untouched Himalayan landscapes, Nyishi villages, and emerging connectivity under development programmes.
facts: One of the most remote circles; visited by Governor in 2024
Recently connected by road; part of Vibrant Village Programme areas
Characterized by dense forests, hills, and traditional settlements
Offers extreme offbeat exploration of northern Kra Daadi

name: Koloriang
description: District headquarters and small hill town of Kurung Kumey, set in a scenic valley on the left bank of the Kurung River, surrounded by high mountains, known for nature walks, trekking, and emerging tourism potential including claims as a contender for the wettest place.
facts: Headquarters of Kurung Kumey district; elevation about 1000-1040 m
Located about 257 km from Itanagar; connected via NH13 / Trans-Arunachal Highway
Coordinates from Wikipedia (27°55′N 93°21′E)
Nyishi tribal area; Longte and Nyokum festivals; potential for nature and cultural tourism
Locals promote it as a possible wettest place on Earth

name: Luru Hugu
description: High-altitude area along the Koloriang-Damin road receiving regular snowfall, emerging as a popular tourist destination for snow experiences in the Nyishi belt of Kurung Kumey.
facts: Located about two hours drive from Koloriang at over 8000 ft elevation
Snowfall on a stretch of about 12 km; heavier every alternate year
Highlighted by district SP as having potential as one of the biggest tourist attractions in the Nyishi belt
Road improvements enhancing accessibility; closest snow experience for many in the Itanagar region

name: Darmu Pass
description: Remote high pass area featuring a landscape resembling the Seven Lakes of Anini, with nearby sea fossils, offering breathtaking views and emerging trek potential.
facts: Described as having a 7 Lakes (Anini)-like landscape
Road to Darmu being constructed by BRO
Sea fossils reported near Darmu
Part of the high-altitude tourism potential of Kurung Kumey

name: Parsi Parlo (Parsiparlo)
description: Remote circle and village area known for Neolithic archaeological remnants, confluence of rivers, excellent Mahseer angling, and Nyishi cultural landscapes near the border.
facts: Neolithic sites excavated by A.A. Ashraf on terraces near the river
Confluence of Kumey with Parsi and Parlo creeks; known for Mahseer fishing
About 48 km from Koloriang; remote Nyishi hamlet with traditional bamboo houses
Part of tourism potential highlighted for angling and heritage

name: Kurung River
description: Major river giving its name to the district, a tributary of the Subansiri with swift greyish waters in Nyishi folklore, offering rafting, angling, and scenic valley journeys.
facts: One of the two namesake rivers of Kurung Kumey district
In Nyishi folklore, the free-spirited sister river with swifter, ash-coloured waters
Potential for whitewater rafting and angling; flows past Koloriang
Part of the intact wilderness suitable for adventure tourism

name: Kumey River
description: Sister river to the Kurung in local folklore, with clearer waters, abundant fish including Mahseer, and potential for rafting and angling through remote valleys.
facts: Namesake river of the district; tributary of the Subansiri
In folklore, the obedient calmer sister to the Kurung
Abundant fish, especially Mahseer near Parsi Parlo confluence
Explored by kayakers; long flat sections with campsites; dam proposals noted in lower reaches

name: Damin
description: Remote administrative circle and settlement in northern Kurung Kumey near the border, known for stone ruins of ancient settlements, waterfalls, and extreme offbeat exploration.
facts: Circle headquarters; on the road from Koloriang past Luru Hugu
Nearby ruins of unknown human settlement with houses made of stone
Part of emerging tourism circuits like Lohr Bogu-Damin
Traditional Nyishi villages amid rugged terrain

name: World War II Plane Wreckage near Koloriang
description: Remnants of a World War II aircraft wreckage located near Koloriang town, adding historical interest to the area's natural attractions.
facts: Mentioned by local authorities as a point of interest near Koloriang
Part of the broader historical layer of the region from wartime activities
Contributes to the district's emerging heritage tourism potential

name: Stone Ruins near Damin
description: Ruins of an unknown human settlement featuring houses made of stone, located near Damin in Kurung Kumey, representing mysterious historical remnants.
facts: Highlighted as ruins of unknown human settlement near Damin
Houses made of stone in a remote area
Part of the archaeological and historical potential of the district

name: Nyapin
description: Charming circle headquarters and village area in Kurung Kumey known for lush green valleys, cascading waterfalls, and interactions with indigenous Nyishi communities.
facts: Administrative circle in Kurung Kumey district
Described in tourism sources for valleys, waterfalls, and snow-capped peaks
Offers cultural immersion with local tribes
Part of the lesser-visited landscapes suitable for nature lovers

name: Sarli
description: Serene administrative circle and block in Kurung Kumey, representing rural Nyishi beauty, traditional lifestyles, and remote Himalayan settings.
facts: Circle in Kurung Kumey; connected by strategic roads including to Huri
Immersive rural beauty amid forests and hills
Part of the district's cultural and nature-based offbeat tourism
Nyishi and other tribal communities

name: Sangram
description: Administrative circle and settlement serving as a base for exploring surrounding Nyishi villages, forests, and river valleys in Kurung Kumey.
facts: SDO headquarters area in the district
Noted in tourism descriptions for nearby villages and cultural experiences
Accessible from Koloriang for offbeat exploration
Part of the traditional Nyishi landscape
